chapters.title: Chapter 1: Probability, Information Theory, and Evaluation Metrics
chapters.description: Introduces basic probability and information-theoretic concepts used to formulate and evaluate sequence models, with emphasis on metrics used in language modeling.
subtopics: Random variables and joint/conditional distributions
Likelihood, log-likelihood, and maximum likelihood estimation
Cross-entropy and KL divergence
Entropy and information content
Perplexity and its relation to cross-entropy
Evaluation protocols for autoregressive models (validation/test splits, tokenization effects)
Statistical significance and confidence intervals for model comparison

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Linear Algebra and Matrix Calculus for Machine Learning
chapters.description: Presents the linear algebra and matrix calculus fundamentals required to follow model definitions and derivations involving vectors, matrices, and outer-product updates.
subtopics: Vectors, matrices, and basic matrix operations
Matrix multiplication, transpose, trace, and Frobenius norm
Outer product, rank, and low-rank approximations
Eigenvalues, singular value decomposition (SVD)
Differentiation with respect to vectors and matrices (matrix derivatives)
Jacobians and gradients for common neural network layers
Complexity of matrix operations (flops, memory)

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Foundations of Neural Networks and Optimization
chapters.description: Covers feedforward neural networks, activation functions, loss functions and the optimization algorithms commonly used in deep learning.
subtopics: Multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and universal approximation
Common activation functions (ReLU, tanh, sigmoid, softmax) and their derivatives
Loss functions for classification and regression
Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and momentum
Adaptive optimizers (Adam, RMSProp) and hyperparameters
Learning rate schedules, warmup, weight decay
Gradient clipping and gradient noise considerations

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Numerical Stability and Normalization Techniques
chapters.description: Discusses numerical issues that arise in deep models (overflow/underflow, large exponentials) and the normalization methods used to stabilize training and inference.
subtopics: Floating-point representation and sources of numerical instability
Log-sum-exp trick and stabilized exponentials
Batch Normalization, Layer Normalization, and Group Normalization
Pre-LayerNorm vs Post-LayerNorm residual blocks
Scaling and bias initialization strategies to control gate behavior
Clipping, scaling and other pragmatic stabilizers used in practice

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Recurrent Neural Networks and Backpropagation Through Time
chapters.description: Introduces RNNs, the unrolled computational graph for sequences, and training via Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT), including vanishing and exploding gradient phenomena.
subtopics: Vanilla RNN formulation and unrolling across time
Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) and truncated BPTT
Vanishing and exploding gradients: causes and implications
Techniques to mitigate gradient issues (clipping, initialization)
Expressive power and limitations of simple RNNs
Computational/time complexity and memory trade-offs for RNN training

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Networks
chapters.description: Presents the canonical LSTM architecture, its gating mechanisms, variants, and the motivations behind the design choices that address BPTT challenges.
subtopics: LSTM cell equations: input, forget, output gates and cell state
Constant error carousel and how LSTM mitigates vanishing gradients
Common LSTM variants (peephole connections, GRU overview) and multi-cell/vectorized LSTM
Gate activation functions and their role
Recurrent weight matrices and memory mixing across cells
Empirical behaviors and typical use-cases of LSTMs

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Gating Mechanisms and Gated Architectures
chapters.description: Examines the role of gating in neural sequence models, different forms of gates, and how they control information flow and dynamics.
subtopics: Motivation for gating: selective memory, gradient control
Sigmoid and hard-sigmoid gates, multiplicative gating
Gated Linear Units (GLU), Highway networks, and variants
Gate parameterization: input-dependent vs hidden-dependent gating
Interactions between multiple gates and their initialization
Practical considerations: saturation, gradient flow, regularization

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Attention Mechanisms and Transformer Architecture
chapters.description: Covers self-attention, multi-head attention, and the Transformer architecture that underpins modern large language models.
subtopics: Scaled dot-product attention: queries, keys, values
Softmax attention, attention weights and interpretation
Multi-head attention: motivation and implementation
Positional encodings and handling sequence order
Transformer block structure, residual connections and layer norm
Computational and memory cost of self-attention (quadratic complexity)

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Linear and Efficient Attention Approaches
chapters.description: Reviews methods that aim to reduce the quadratic cost of attention to linear or near-linear, including kernelized and low-rank approximations.
subtopics: Kernelized attention and random feature approximations (Performer)
Linear Transformer and factorized attention methods
Linformer and low-rank attention approximations
Sparse attention and locality-biased mechanisms
Practical trade-offs: approximation error vs efficiency
Comparisons of asymptotic cost and empirical performance

chapters.title: Chapter 10: State-Space Models for Sequence Modeling
chapters.description: Introduces linear state-space models and their modern neural parameterizations used for long-range sequence modeling.
subtopics: Discrete-time linear state-space equations
Interpretation of SSMs as sequence filters or convolutions
Parameterizations used in S4, DSS, S5 and related models
Connections between SSMs and convolutional/filtering views
Advantages and limitations (linear complexity, expressivity)
Training and implementation details (diagonalization, FFT-based approaches)

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Fast Weights, Hebbian Learning, and Associative Memories
chapters.description: Covers classical and modern approaches to associative memory using outer-product updates and fast-weight mechanisms.
subtopics: Hebbian learning and basic associative memory ideas
Bidirectional Associative Memories (BAM) and Hopfield networks
Outer-product (covariance) update rules and their properties
Fast Weight Programmers and the historical lineage
Capacity, interference, and normalization in associative memories
Modern instantiations: fast-weight attention, retrieval dynamics

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Key-Value Memory Architectures and Retrieval
chapters.description: Examines explicit memory modules that store and retrieve key-value pairs, covering retrieval mechanics and capacity considerations.
subtopics: Key-value memories: keys, queries, and read/write operations
Dot-product retrieval and normalization strategies
Memory capacity, collisions and noise (signal-to-noise analysis)
Decay / forgetting mechanisms and plasticity
Caching strategies (KV-cache) for autoregressive decoding
Benchmarks and tasks emphasizing associative recall

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Residual Networks, Deep Architectures, and Block Design
chapters.description: Presents residual connections and common block designs that enable training of very deep networks, including pre/post normalization choices.
subtopics: Residual learning and identity skip connections
Pre-LayerNorm vs Post-LayerNorm residual blocks
Design patterns for transformer-like and SSM-like blocks
Projection (up/down) and bottleneck layers
Effects of depth on optimization and expressivity
Practical considerations: stability, initialization and scaling

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Complexity, Parallelization, and GPU Implementation Basics
chapters.description: Covers computational complexity analysis and basic GPU/CUDA concepts relevant to implementing large sequence models efficiently.
subtopics: Time and memory complexity with respect to sequence length and model dimension
Data and model parallelism strategies
Batching, streaming and incremental decoding
GPU programming primitives (kernels, warps, registers, shared memory)
KV-caches and memory trade-offs in autoregressive generation
Practical profiling and bottleneck analysis

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Mixed-Precision Training and Numerical Optimization Tricks
chapters.description: Discusses mixed-precision training, stability techniques when training large models, and practical optimizer considerations.
subtopics: FP32, FP16 and BF16 numeric formats and trade-offs
Automatic mixed precision (AMP) and loss scaling
Optimizer state handling with reduced precision
Checkpointing, gradient accumulation and memory saving
Warmup schedules and conservative hyperparameter choices for large-scale runs
Reproducibility and deterministic training considerations

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Scaling Laws and Large Language Model Design
chapters.description: Introduces empirical scaling laws for model size, dataset size, and compute, and implications for the design and evaluation of large language models.
subtopics: Empirical scaling laws (Kaplan et al.) and power-law fits
Trade-offs between model size, dataset size, and compute budget
Chinchilla scaling and data/model compute-optimal regimes
Practical implications for training regimes and dataset curation
Evaluation regimes for scaled models (downstream tasks, zero/few-shot)
Limitations and caveats of scaling laws

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Theoretical Principles for High-Dimensional Representations
chapters.description: Presents theory motivating high-dimensional nonlinear embeddings and their ability to separate patterns (Cover's theorem) and related representational arguments.
subtopics: Cover's theorem on separability in high dimensions
Nonlinear feature maps and kernel perspectives
Embedding dimensionality, overparameterization and expressivity
Trade-offs between capacity and generalization in high dimensions
Practical use of up-/down-projections in block designs

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Sequence Modeling Tasks, Benchmarks, and Experimental Methodology
chapters.description: Describes commonly used synthetic tasks and real-world benchmarks to stress-test sequence models, along with rigorous experimental practices.
subtopics: Synthetic tasks: associative recall, copy, parity, formal languages
Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark and its task suite
Language modeling datasets (wikitext, SlimPajama) and tokenization issues
PALOMA and other domain evaluation suites
Metrics and evaluation procedures for length extrapolation
Ablation studies and controlled comparisons

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Statistical Learning, Generalization, and Overfitting in Sequence Models
chapters.description: Covers principles of generalization for sequence models, regularization strategies and diagnosing overfitting in large models.
subtopics: Bias-variance trade-off in high-capacity sequence models
Regularization techniques (dropout, weight decay, data augmentation)
Early stopping, validation strategies and hyperparameter tuning
Catastrophic forgetting and continual learning considerations
Measuring and interpreting model calibration and confidence
Benchmarking robustness across domains and lengths

chapters.title: Chapter 20: Historical and Conceptual Foundations of Memory in Neural Systems
chapters.description: Surveys classical literature and conceptual frameworks for memory in neural computation that inform modern memory-augmented models.
subtopics: Early associative memory models (Hopfield, BAM, Kohonen networks)
Hebbian principles and covariance-based learning
Psychological and neuroscientific motivations for gating and working memory
Fast weights and temporary synaptic changes in historical context
Connections between classical associative memories and modern neural architectures
Limitations and theoretical bounds of associative memory models
